summary: E0 (initial_measurements.json) shows similar t=0 segmented empty-area fractions in A and B, followed by lower values in A (~0.0044 at 24 h) and increasing B values (~0.0892 at 24 h). These are image area fractions, not concentrations or free energies; seven fields are nested within two preparations. Candidate C1 proposes that B develops internal RNA-poor cavities when transcription-driven junction accumulation outruns network relaxation, trapping solvent-rich regions that then become mechanically arrested. This is an explicitly new, unconfirmed mechanism hypothesis, not an inference from the area-fraction curve. Reduced state x is load-bearing junction density (dimensionless effective fraction); r(t) is transcriptional production flux per droplet volume (h^-1 in this reduced model); tau is network relaxation time (h). Adopt xdot = alpha r(t) - x/tau, with alpha dimensionless. Define arrest threshold x_c and cavity state q: qdot = k_n max(x-x_c,0) - k_d q while x < x_c, and qdot = 0 after x first reaches x_c (arrest). Here q is cavity area fraction, k_n and k_d have units h^-1, and the post-threshold freeze is a proposed reduced rule, not established physics. It predicts a rate/history effect: at equal integrated production, a sufficiently fast pulse can cross x_c while a slow schedule does not; after arrest, q persists when production falls. Meaningful alternative C_alt is equilibrium composition-driven demixing: after matching final composition and allowing equilibration, cavity fraction should not depend on production schedule. E0 alone cannot distinguish these, identify x, show arrest, or establish amplification as causal.

candidates.target: Delayed emergence and persistence of segmented internal RNA-poor cavities in transcribing RNA droplets, particularly the B versus A contrast.
known_relations: E0: at t=0 A=0.01487 and B=0.01381; by 24 h A=0.00446 and B=0.08918 in mean segmented empty-area fraction.
E0 measures area fractions. It does not measure RNA concentration, composition, free energy, network relaxation, or cavity motion.
A/B differ by amplification treatment, whose effects on template sequence, purity, and carryover are not identified.
hypotheses: H1 (new, unconfirmed): B enters a kinetic-arrest regime because transcription-driven accumulation of load-bearing RNA junctions exceeds network relaxation; solvent-rich cavities form above a threshold and become trapped when the network arrests.
H2 (alternative): amplification-linked composition or product heterogeneity changes equilibrium phase coexistence, producing cavities without a production-rate-dependent arrest threshold.
H3 (alternative causal path): reaction carryover or imaging/segmentation changes associated with preparation account for some or all of the difference.

gaps.description: Missing relation: under what conditions can ongoing production and slow relaxation of an associating RNA network generate internal solvent-rich domains and arrest their coarsening, and what rate/history dependence follows? A result supporting a threshold or arrest under compatible conditions would motivate H1; evidence that such conditions are incompatible would weaken it.
A/B causal attribution is unresolved among altered template/product populations, carryover, and measurement differences.
No direct measurements of junction density, relaxation time, phase composition, or cavity trajectories are supplied.

candidates.initial_boundary_conditions: x(0)=x0 in [0,1], q(0)=observed initial area fraction only under the unvalidated mapping; r(t)>=0. No spatial boundary or droplet geometry is supplied. This reduced model has no conservation claim for total RNA or solvent.
candidates.observation_mapping: Only y_area, the segmented internal dark area divided by filled droplet area, is currently measured. It is not RNA concentration and need not equal a material volume fraction. SEM and object counts do not provide preparation-level replication. No fit is claimed.
alternatives: C_alt equilibrium composition-driven phase separation: at matched final composition after equilibration, predicted cavity fraction is schedule-independent.
C_alt2 amplification-related reaction carryover can alter transcription or imaging independently of sequence/network arrest.
C_alt3 segmentation or denominator changes can alter y_area without equivalent changes in physical cavity volume.
predictions: For a production pulse and a slower schedule with equal integrated production and matched final composition, H1 predicts cavity formation only in the schedule whose x(t) crosses x_c; C_alt predicts convergence after equilibration.
If H1 arrest has occurred, decreasing production after threshold crossing does not promptly erase q; before threshold crossing, q decays with timescale 1/k_d when x<=x_c.
Under a constant rate r, x approaches alpha*r*tau from below; threshold crossing is possible only if alpha*r*tau>x_c. This is a conditional consequence, not an estimated property of A or B.
checks: Dimensional check: alpha*r and x/tau both have units h^-1; each term in qdot has units h^-1 because q and x are dimensionless.
Threshold limit: if alpha*r*tau<=x_c from x0 below threshold, the model predicts no newly generated cavities; if r=0, x decays exponentially with time constant tau.
Persistence is produced by the stated post-threshold arrest rule, so it is a distinct testable assumption, not a derivation from known RNA physics.
Measurement compatibility is unresolved: q is provisionally equated to an area fraction, not a concentration or volume fraction.
E0 trend is directionally compatible with delayed cavity growth in B but does not test x, threshold crossing, persistence after production stops, or schedule dependence.
evidence_conflicts: The small initial difference and later B increase are compatible with delayed emergence, but field-pooled SEMs cannot establish preparation-level significance or causal mechanism.
No supplied evidence measures production rate, sequence heterogeneity, phase composition, or motion; alternatives remain live.
